newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ABN AMRO denies fraud report in Dutch paper.
newsitem.headline: ABN AMRO denies fraud report in Dutch paper.

text.p: Dutch bank ABN AMRO NV on Friday denied a report in the Dutch Telegraaf daily newspaper that it had been the victim of a 185 million guilder fraud involving the transfer of money abroad.

"The newspaper is referring to a case we discovered last November and that has already been reported by the media, related to administrative irregularities at one of our Amsterdam branches," ABN AMRO spokesman Jules Prast said.
"It's difficult for us to establish how much has been involved, and it will amount to millions of guilders, but it's definitely not the 185 million the paper talks about," he said.
Prast said four staff handling business accounts related to the Amsterdam diamond trade had been suspended from the Sarphatti Street branch in central Amsterdam last November.
He said unauthorised transfers and credits had been discovered and that the investigation would continue, probably for some months.

ABN AMRO had routine provisions available to deal with such cases and was in any case insured, said Prast, adding that as an extra measure it took out added provisions last year after discovering the affair.

Prast said there was no question of clients being out of pocket because of the affair and said there would be no noticeable effect on the bank's 1996 results which are due to be announced on February 27.
"We want to say that in the face of ludicrous amounts of money being named that this is a totally manageable thing and it will have no effect of any significance on the 1996 results," said Prast.
